title: Batcher Insights + Heuristic Controller for Continuous Batching
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's automatic batching and KV-prefix caching deliver large token-cost savings, but current recommendations are manual, brittle, and require ops intervention for safe application. This ticket designs and implements a 'Batcher Insights' service plus a Heuristic Controller that: collects workload profiles, computes candidate continuous-batching parameters and cache policies, scores safety/cost trade-offs, and supports a controlled apply/rollback path (canary -> gradual rollout -> instant rollback).

Proposal summary:
1) Workload profiler: lightweight agent in the serving runtime that emits per-route, per-model histograms (sequence length, request inter-arrival, token distribution, prefix reuse ratio, cached-kv-hit-rate) at 1m granularity. Data is aggregated to S3 and a short retention ClickHouse table for near-term analysis.
2) Heuristic scoring engine: offline batch that consumes profile blobs and produces candidate config deltas (batch_limits, max_prefetch_ms, cache_window_seconds, aggressive_prefix_merge boolean). Heuristics encode safety rules (latency impact thresholds, p99 token-latency < SLO delta, memory headroom guardrails).
3) Continuous-batching controller: an orchestration layer that can propose configs as 'suggested', run a canary against 1-5% traffic, measure a short set of safety metrics, and either promote, roll back or refine the candidate. All applied configs are versioned and can be auto-rolled back on SLA regression.

Key trade-offs considered:
- Conservative safety thresholds reduce cost upside but avoid production regressions. We choose default thresholds that favor latency SLO, with a tuning knob per-customer.
- Profiling frequency vs. overhead: 1m aggregates chosen to balance signal and CPU/RT overhead.
- Offline heuristics vs. learned models: we start with deterministic heuristics (more predictable) and add a lightweight learned ranking model in a follow-up.

Data schema (summary):
- profile_id: string (route|model|timewindow)
- seq_len_hist: base64-encoded compressed histogram
- interarrival_q: p50,p90,p99
- prefix_reuse_pct: float
- kv_cache_hit: float
- concurrent_rps: int
- memory_headroom_bytes: int

Telemetry & gating metrics (canary evaluation):
- cost_per_100k_tokens delta (expected savings vs. baseline)
- p50/p95/p99 token-latency change (must be < configured thresholds)
- error-rate (5xx + application errors) change
- tail_cpu & memory headroom
- cache-eviction-rate change

Safe apply/rollback plan:
- Step 1: Suggest candidate in Console with projected cost delta and risk band.
- Step 2: Canary apply to 1% traffic for 30 minutes; collect telemetry and compare to control using pre-registered queries.
- Step 3: If canary passes (all gating metrics within thresholds), auto-promote to 25% for another 30m; otherwise auto-rollback to previous config and generate alert + incident link.
- Step 4: Gradual ramp to 100% over configurable windows, with auto-stop on regressions.

API & UX surface:
- Console: 'Batcher Insights' page with per-route suggestions, confidence score, projected monthly savings, and 'Apply (Canary)' CTA.
- REST: POST /v1/batching/suggest -> returns candidates, POST /v1/batching/apply with {mode: canary|gradual|force}.
- Audit logs stored in Private control plane for customers with Private deployments.

Rollout & guardrails:
- Default global threshold: p99 token-latency increase <= 5% absolute or 50ms (whichever is smaller).
- For enterprise customers, allow 'aggressive' profile that increases thresholds when SLA allows.
- All auto-applies are opt-in per-organization.

Operational notes:
- Housekeeping job to expire old profile blobs after 90 days.
- Use feature flag to enable controller on staging first.

acceptance_criteria: Profiler agent emits required fields to metrics aggregation and sample blobs are visible in the S3 test bucket
Offline heuristic engine runs end-to-end on weekly synthetic workloads and produces candidate JSON with expected fields
Controller can apply canary configs and revert automatically based on gating queries
Console surfaces at least one suggestion per high-traffic route in the staging org
End-to-end e2e test that simulates regression triggers automated rollback and creates an incident ticket

Console UI: suggestions list, apply canary flow, explainability modal
Create gating dashboards & pre-baked queries for canary evaluation
Write runbook: rollback playbook + alerting rules
Staging rollout behind feature flag; smoke tests and chaos test
